issues.legal_issue: An appeal against the remaining defendants may proceed when it has been dismissed as against a respondent who is not a necessary party.
material_facts: The plaintiffs appealed the dismissal of their suit and included the deity as a respondent, although they sought no relief against it.
The appeal was dismissed as against the deity because the plaintiffs did not pay the guardian’s costs.
No party to the appeal had died.
issues.conclusion: The appeal had not abated, either wholly or in part, and the plaintiffs could prosecute it against the contesting defendants without the deity.
issues.legal_principle: A dismissal of an appeal as against a respondent who is not a necessary party does not make the appeal incompetent against the other respondents. Abatement does not arise where no party has died.

rule.if: civil_appeal and respondent_not_necessary_party and appeal_dismissed_as_to_respondent_for_costs and no_party_died

predicates.civil_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal from a civil suit.
predicates.respondent_not_necessary_party: The respondent against whom the appeal was dismissed was not necessary to determine the relief sought against the other respondents.
predicates.appeal_dismissed_as_to_respondent_for_co: The appeal was dismissed as against that respondent because the appellant did not pay the costs required for the respondent’s representation.
predicates.no_party_died: No party to the appeal died.
predicates.appeal_remains_competent_against_other_p: The appeal may proceed against the other parties.

issues.definition: When a civil appeal is dismissed as against a non-necessary respondent for non-payment of representation costs and no party has died, it may still proceed against the other parties.

issues.legal_issue: A decision on an issue between co-defendants does not operate as res judicata between them when that issue has not been finally decided between them.
material_facts: The trial court decided that the disputed lands did not appertain to the village of which the deity was proprietor.
The plaintiffs appealed, bringing that question again before the appellate court.
The appeal was dismissed as against the deity before the appellate court decided the merits, and the appellate court made no merits decision on the issue in the deity’s presence.
issues.conclusion: The trial court’s decision did not finally determine the issue between the deity and the contesting defendants, so it did not operate as res judicata between them.
issues.legal_principle: Under Muni Bibi v. Trilokinath, L.R. 58 I.A. 158, res judicata between co-defendants requires a conflict of interest between them, the necessity of deciding that conflict to grant the plaintiff relief, and a final decision of the question between the co-defendants. The third condition was not satisfied here; filing the appeal brought the question back into judicial inquiry, and no final merits decision was made against the deity.

predicates.civil_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal from a civil suit.
predicates.prior_decision_under_appeal: The trial court decided the issue that is again before the appellate court.
predicates.issue_not_finally_decided_between_codefe: The issue between the co-defendants was not finally determined between them before the appeal was disposed of.

issues.definition: When a civil appeal brings a trial-court decision back for review and the issue between co-defendants was not finally decided between them, the earlier decision is not res judicata between those co-defendants.

issues.legal_issue: Land that originally belonged to proprietors remains theirs when it is lost by river recession and later reforms in situ, absent proof that another claimant acquired title.
material_facts: The disputed lands originally belonged to the proprietors of the villages from which they were lost by river action.
The lands reformed in situ after the river receded.
The plaintiffs did not prove that the deity came into possession of the lands as alleged or otherwise establish title to them.
issues.conclusion: The property in the lands remained with the original proprietors, the plaintiffs failed to establish title, and the suit and appeal had no merit.
issues.legal_principle: Applying the findings in the companion appeal, the Court held that where the lands originally belonged to the proprietors and reformed in situ after river recession, their property remained with those proprietors. The Court also relied on the plaintiffs’ failure to prove the deity’s possession or the plaintiffs’ title.

predicates.civil_title_appeal: The proceeding is a civil appeal concerning title to land.
predicates.land_originally_belonged_to_other_propri: The land originally belonged to proprietors other than the claimant.
predicates.land_reformed_in_situ_after_river_recess: After a river receded, the land reformed in its original location.
predicates.claimant_failed_to_prove_title: The claimant did not prove title to the land.
predicates.title_remains_with_original_proprietors: Title to the land remains with its original proprietors.

issues.definition: If a claimant fails to prove title to land that originally belonged to other proprietors and reformed in situ after river recession, title remains with those proprietors.

issues.legal_issue: A claim of acquisition of title by adverse possession cannot be raised for the first time at the appellate stage when it was not an issue at trial.
material_facts: There was no trial issue about whether the deity had acquired title to the lands by adverse possession.
The plaintiffs sought to raise that claim at the appellate stage.
The plaintiffs did not establish that the deity had acquired title to any part of the lands by adverse possession.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiffs could not raise the adverse-possession claim for the first time on appeal and failed to establish acquisition of title by adverse possession.
issues.legal_principle: A plea of acquisition of title by adverse possession cannot be raised for the first time at the appellate stage when no issue on it was tried below.

predicates.civil_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal from a civil suit.
predicates.no_trial_issue_on_adverse_possession: The trial did not include an issue about acquisition of title by adverse possession.
predicates.adverse_possession_plea_raised_first_on_: The claimant raised the adverse-possession plea for the first time in the appeal.
predicates.adverse_possession_plea_cannot_be_raised: The adverse-possession plea cannot be raised for the first time at the appellate stage.

issues.definition: When an adverse-possession claim was not an issue at trial and is raised for the first time in a civil appeal, it cannot be raised for the first time at that stage.
